steps.content: [Background - Clementine's Study]

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Surprise! Didn't see that coming, did you?
Clementine beams at you. Seems like she's very proud of her little trick.

options: Unfortunately for you, I did see that coming.

steps.content: Writing yourself into your own book... does that count as "drawing inspiration from reality"?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Now then, what do you think I'm trying to do? Care to take a guess?

It can't simply be to save herself the trouble of coming up with another name. Though, rather than the author's questionable sense of humor, you're more concerned with what new case this book might lead to.
You continue reading, returning to the train corridor and to the side of that slightly unfamiliar "Clementine" within the pages...
[Background - Train Corridor]

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: ${PlayerName}, don't just stand there. Aren't you going to come to my room?
The woman appears from behind you. She takes your arm, her body drawing close in a motion so clean it seems rehearsed.
She clearly knows you, but you've never met her before.

steps.speaker: Train Attendant
steps.content: Ms. Clementine! Are the two of you together...?

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: No, I don't know—
You instinctively want to deny it, but her grip on your arm tightens before you can finish speaking. The woman answers before you can.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Are there no tickets left? Why didn't you come find me sooner? I've been waiting inside for ages, you know. That's very mean of you.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: If you just need a room, why not come to my compartment? There's more than enough space for two.

Clementine begins pulling you toward the carriage before she even finishes talking. Her movements are so natural that the attendant couldn't react at first, freezing for half a second before remembering to object.

steps.speaker: Train Attendant
steps.content: Wait, ma'am! This isn't proper according to regulations—
The attendant's words are cut short by the banknotes flung at her.
The bills scatter through the air as Clementine lowers her hand, her expression relaxed. One would think she'd merely tossed away a used napkin.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: I get it. It's about the money, right? Go ahead — you can have it all.
You want to stay and keep watching, but the woman beside you forcibly pulls you away.

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: Bribing our way in like that... is a bit inappropriate, isn't it...?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: My, there's no need to worry. People like that can't say no to money.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: If you're really that concerned, though, you can just move to another seat once someone gets off later. It'd be better than sleeping on a hard bench, right?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: And don't you have business to attend to? I'd venture to guess you wouldn't want to miss the train over this.
She winks at you, her grin widening as she continues:

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Not to mention... I still need to discuss a case with you, my dear <color=#fb9259>detective</color>.
Clementine gives you no chance to refuse.

You frown, but you still let her pull you deeper into the corridor. You don't approve of her methods, but alas, your principles are too insignificant before the thought of spending two nights on a hard bench.
Besides, according to what she said, you might even have the chance to pick up another job on this train.
[Background - Suite Parlor]
With the attendant's help, your luggage is brought to Clementine's compartment.
Besides the partitioned bedroom, the compartment has an area similar to a living room. In its center sits a plush, luxurious sofa—no doubt extremely comfortable to lie on.
Clearly, Clementine has no shortage of cash. Her compartment is easily twice the size of anyone else's.
You've barely found your footing when a long whistle blares from overhead.
The train has started moving.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Have a seat. Don't be shy, make yourself at home.
Clementine steps into the room and immediately flops onto the seat as if all tension has left her body. Seeing you still standing, she pats the spot beside her, gesturing for you to sit.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Care for a drink? Some tea, perhaps? If you need anything, just ring for service. Feel free to put it on my tab.

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: Thank you, but one night is more than enough. Hopefully, they'll have a room available soon.
But before your little chat continues, you have more pressing questions that need answering—

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: How did you recognize me? I don't believe I've worked on any cases with you involved, so why did you help me?
You do have a small reputation as a detective, but you're hardly a household name. Most people might have heard your name, but they wouldn't be able to recognize you on sight.
Unless... she knew you were coming.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Hmm...
The woman rubs her chin, seemingly lost in thought for a moment, before clapping her hands together.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Detectives are supposed to be quite smart, right? Why don't you take a guess? If you guess right, I'll tell you the answer.
What kind of logic is that? If you could guess the answer, what's the point of having her repeat it? Well, beggars can't be choosers—even a detective has to humor their host.

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: First, while your coat has no ostentatious embellishments, the stitching, fabric, and cuff work all suggest it was crafted by a master tailor. You must be considerably wealthy.

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: On top of that, this badge gives away your identity.
You point to the coffee table beside the sofa, and Clementine looks in the same direction, following your gesture. An ornate metal badge lies on its surface.

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: A scale entwined with vines—this badge belongs to a discreet but affluent family. Seldom known to the public, but they've produced numerous influential figures in the world of politics, nonetheless.

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: If you're connected to this family, learning about me would be a trivial matter.
Clementine's eyes widen, visibly surprised, as she applauds your deduction.

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: But there's still one thing I don't quite understand.

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: If you merely wanted to hire me, you could have contacted me directly. After all, anyone can find my address in the morning papers. What's more, with your connections, you could easily find detectives far more accomplished than myself. Unless...

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: Something you couldn't anticipate happened on this train only after you boarded it. <color=#fb9259>Something significant enough that you had no choice but to seek out a detective</color>.
As you lay out your deduction, Clementine leans forward, her eyes sparkling. The sight fills you with unease.
You've seen this look before on the faces of troublemakers—excitement, obsession, hunger. People like this always cause disasters on a whim, dragging everyone around them into the mess.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Bingo! As expected of a professional detective. That was very impressive!

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: This wretched train is way too slow. It takes two whole days just to arrive at the destination. I was wondering how I'd pass the time, but look what fate has brought me! How delightful!
Looks like your intuition was right. This woman's trouble.

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: ...What do you mean? What do you want from me?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: I have a case for you. It has to do with—

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: <color=#fb9259>A murder that is about to take place</color> on the train.
[Doyle's Office]

Meanwhile

Public Security Bureau, Eastside
Somewhere in Eastside, a weary inspector was about to surface from the ocean of case files on his desk for a breath of air when his terminal buzzed, cutting his respite short.
He answers the call. A familiar voice comes through from the other end. At first, the man listens with impatience, but his frown deepens with each passing moment.
Long after the call ends, he finally lets out a heavy sigh, opens his computer, enters his password, and logs into the Public Security Bureau's internal network.
